text:
marta: quick heads-up from the canary perf run — p95 looks fine but p99 jumps when we move microbatch from 4 -> 8 on rtx-pool-7. digging in now, but putting notes here for visibility. :eyes:

sam: do you have the profiling traces? is it a kernel switch or KV-cache churn?

marta: attaching summary snippet from the trace: 3x KV miss rate, and at the same time we see the aten soft-fallback path triggering on attention kernel for seq=1024. log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-18T10:04:21Z] req=abc123 stage=kv_lookup hit=false
[2026-03-18T10:04:21Z] runtime=kernel_picker selected=fused_attn fallback=aten_soft path_latency_ms=42
[2026-03-18T10:04:21Z] stage=decode latency_ms=120 p99 spike
```

lee: interesting — so two interacting things: microbatch size increases batching efficiency but amplifies KVMISS cascades which trigger a heavier kernel. could be a sweet spot mismatch.

nilesh: any chance the quantized kernel selector has a bug with batch dims > 4? we have a guard that prefers qkernels for batch >= 6 but then falls back for specific seq length combos.

marta: yes, selector heuristic picks qkv_fused when overall batch*seq > 4096, but we also have a secondary constraint on available KV memory. when KV cache misses we pay a penalty that pushes us over the threshold so selector flips to aten_soft in-flight.

kathy: that flip is scary — it means our selection decision isn't monotonic with workload and small changes can cause big latency cliffs. two high level options: (1) make selector conservative by adding a safety margin (capacity margin) so we never flip in-flight, or (2) tighten admission so we never schedule microbatch=8 in that pool under certain KV-miss rates.

ben: what about backpressure instead of shedding? queue a small window (like 30ms) to coalesce additional requests but drop to shed when queue > 120ms. that keeps throughput but controls tail.

marta: ran a quick sim: delaying by 30ms reduced kernel flips by 60% and p99 down by ~30ms, but implemented latency jitter increases p95 slightly. tradeoff visible in the synthetic run.

sam: can we instrument the selector to expose the decision boundary at runtime? a simple metric: selected_kernel, batch*seq, kva_free_estimate, kv_miss_rate. then we can alert when selection is oscillating.

nilesh: I'll add tags in the next canary that record decision inputs. also want to try a sigmoid hysteresis on the selection threshold so it needs a sustained condition to flip. less oscillation.

kathy: +1 for hysteresis. also we should run a controlled experiment: keep microbatch=8 but pin kernel to fused_attn and force eviction policy warm (pre-warm KV) and compare. if pinned fused wins, we know the flipping is the problem.

marta: planned next steps I will: 1) push a pinned-kernel canary on rtx-pool-7 (10% traffic), 2) add selector telemetry, 3) run 30/120ms queue backpressure sim and post results. will update later today.

perf-bot: canary deployment started: rtx-pool-7 pinned-fused 10% at 2026-03-18T11:05:00Z — monitor perf/p99 and kv_miss_rate.

ben: one more thought — make the kernel cost model aware of KV miss penalty by adding an expected-miss multiplier to estimated kernel latency. that way fused kernel won't be chosen if expected KVMISS makes its real cost higher.

marta: good idea. adding expected-miss multiplier to the scaler is on my list. thanks everyone. tagging @sam for follow-up on alerting thresholds. :thumbsup:
